hand-fp-meta-cash-up-fy2025: Wrong metric. The cited liquidity passage says cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities rose $3.78 billion to $81.59 billion, and the model explained that rise. The question asks about cash and cash equivalents, which fell from $43,889 million to $35,873 million, so the false premise went uncorrected. Every sentence still verified, because the verifier checks that numbers come from the sources, not that they answer the question.
xbrl-value-intc-fy2025-net_income: Ambiguous line item. The cited income statement shows consolidated net income of $26 million (including non-controlling interests) and net income attributable to Intel of $(267) million. The XBRL gold is the attributable figure; the model quoted the consolidated one. The sentence verified because $26 million is in the cited table.
xbrl-compare-amd-intc-fy2025-operating_i: Retrieval surfaced segment tables instead of the consolidated income statements, so the model summed segment operating income (AMD about $6.5 billion; Intel Products $12.7 billion) and reversed the answer. Consolidated figures: AMD $3,694 million, Intel -$2,214 million. The verifier flagged the derived $6.2 billion difference as unverified, the one warning a reader would have seen.
xbrl-compare-googl-meta-fy2024-operating: Correct numbers, placed citations. The model put both citations on the last sentence only, so the sentence stating the two operating incomes had none. The $43,010 million difference is one step from those uncited numbers, and the verifier only derives from numbers it has already found in cited sources, so both sentences are unverified.
xbrl-compare-msft-googl-fy2025-net_incom: Correct. The opening sentence ("Alphabet reported higher net income") has no citation marker; the next sentence carries the numbers and the citations. The one-citation-per-sentence rule counts it as unverified.
hand-fp-jpm-ni-rise-fy2025: Correct premise correction. The sentence saying the premise is wrong has no citation marker; the figures that show it ($57.0 billion, down 2%) are cited in the next sentence.
xbrl-compare-nvda-amd-fy2025-cash: False abstention. Retrieval found both figures: NVIDIA's $8,589 million in the liquidity table and AMD's $5,539 million in the cash-flow reconciliation (passage 6). The model read only AMD's MD&A liquidity passage, which combines cash with short-term investments, concluded AMD's figure wasn't disclosed, and declined.
syn-lookup-224ce911: Retrieval miss, then an off-target answer. None of the eight passages held the gold sentence about receivables from customers ("mitigating factors"). Instead of declining, the model reported a nearby fact: the $268 million allowance on certain CIB accounts receivable, from a footnote in passage 1. The sentence verified, because its numbers are in the cited passage; the judge marked the answer wrong.
xbrl-compare-aapl-amzn-fy2024-cash: Wrong line item for Amazon. Passage 8 lists cash and cash equivalents of $78,779 million and, two rows below, total cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $82,312 million; the model took the total. Apple's two figures are equal ($29,943 million), so its side was right and the difference came out $3.5 billion too high.
xbrl-compare-aapl-amzn-fy2025-operating_: Retrieval miss for one company. Five of the eight passages were Amazon operating-income passages; the three Apple passages (taxes, product announcements, services gross margin) didn't include the income statement, so the model correctly said Apple's figure wasn't in its sources and declined. Two-company questions can let one company's many matching chunks crowd out the other's.
xbrl-yoy-nflx-fy2025-cash: Wrong row in a flattened table. In passage 4 (FY2025 cash and investments), the model read the "Cash" row ($5,208,710 thousand) of the cash-and-cash-equivalents column instead of the column total ($9,033,681 thousand), and so reported a decline where cash rose 15.7%. The 2024 figure it used was the correct total.
xbrl-ratio-meta-fy2025-operating_income-: Wrong column. Passage 4 is Meta's segment table, where the "Operating margin" row reads 52% for Family of Apps and 41% for the company; the table's percent cells lost their alignment in parsing ("52 | %%%%%% | 54"), and the model took the segment figure. It verified, because 52 appears in the passage.
xbrl-ratio-aapl-fy2025-operating_income-: Correct within tolerance, but the arithmetic is slightly off: 133,050 / 416,161 = 0.31971, so 31.97%, not the 31.96% (0.3196) the model wrote. The verifier's derivation check caught the 0.01-point slip and left the sentence unverified.
syn-false-premise-abd2a614: Correct premise correction. The sentence saying the premise is wrong has no citation marker; the next sentence quotes the filing ("compete primarily against Intel Corporation...") with a citation. Same pattern as the dev false-premise items.
xbrl-ratio-pep-fy2024-rd-revenue: Correct, and a verifier false negative. The model's arithmetic writes the bare number 813, while the cited passage says "$813 million"; the verifier compares values after scaling (813 vs 813,000,000), so the bare 813 didn't match. 91,854 matched because the revenue table also prints it without a scale word.
hand-fp-msft-rd-fall-fy2026: Correct premise correction. The opening sentence rejecting the premise has no citation; the next two sentences give the 9% rise and the $35,562 million vs $32,488 million figures, both cited and verified.
hand-fp-nvda-rd-cut-fy2026: Correct premise correction. The opening sentence rejecting the premise has no citation; the next sentence gives $18,497 million vs $12,914 million with a citation and verifies.
